questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Finding a place with a university of which I has heard good things about, and was close to home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. Some of the information could get lost in the emails, but overall I found it easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had an orientationer week, where we would be introduced to the university, classes, the system etc. 
I really appreciated this, as universities can work very differently from each other

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Fairly easy. 
I used Erasmus in Prague, where I along with some others could find a flat. However, one should look into this at the early stages of applying abroad, as good flats are taken quickly

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: one should look into this at the early stages of applying abroad, as good flats are taken quickly, look into what part of the city the acommodations are, and the prises

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to log into a system, where you enroll yourself into the different classes. Then you search the system and enroll yourself, until you have found every one. If the course is full, you cannot enroll.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: During that process you couldnt at the moment get any help. The teachers and responsible people of the different faculties were easy to find on mail, and very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a bunch of 'safety' courses, so you have a few to pick between, if a course you were interested in isn't available when you try to enroll.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were fairly easy. However, my opinion is biased, as I have had a lot of the same theories at my home univerisity

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was kind of the same, with both lectures, where only the teacher spoke, group assignments, and individual assignments all included.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Experimental studies in psychology and education
Educational and school psychology
Equity in Education
Quality in Education
Counseling theory and practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Quality in education and educational and school psychology. I felt that they were good, with a lot of interesting subjects

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A new phone subscription, as I found out I couldnt use the one I had in Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A bunch of different social activities as a Czech ball, different trips and a lot of other things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Erasmus in Prague has a lot of great activities, such as karaoke, boat parties, running clubs and others. It is a great way to meet other exchange students from a lot of different countries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to some of the cities outside Prague, as Kutna Hora, Cesky Krumlov and Brno. 
Take a bus or train to some of the countries nearby Czech Republic

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, if you tried to seek it. However, there are a lot of international people in Prague, so local activities and culture is a bit hader

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging, and didn't notice any particular differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I loved the busyness and calmness of the city at the same time, and the politeness in public.
I loved the city and all the sightings, and especially the parks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find acommodation early on, if you want to live off campus.
Follow Erasmus in Prague on instagram, to find good social activities
Find a lot of different courses in advance, so you have a lot of backup courses if some are not available

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the orientation week activities, cause you can connect with a lot of your peers, and learn a lot about the university and get a good start to the semester

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of people from different countries, with individual experiences, and gaining a lot of new knowledge of other cultures and ways of living

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The adaptation to the new surroundings, university and every day life you have there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
